evidence: src/infrastructure/config/createApp.ts: createApp() is described as the 'Composition root: builds the in-memory stores, use cases and HTTP routes' and creates the products, orders and stock instances once.
src/infrastructure/config/createApp.ts: passes the shared instances through `buildOrderController(orders, stock).routes()` instead of building order use cases itself.

src/infrastructure/config/orderModule.ts: buildOrderController(orders: OrderRepository, stock: StockReservationService) only builds the PlaceOrder, GetOrder, ListOrdersByState, AdvanceOrder and CancelOrder use cases and passes them to OrderController.

src/infrastructure/config/createApp.ts: stock wiring is inline (`new StockController(new ListStockLevelsUseCase(products))`). This is a small asymmetry with the order builder, not duplication or a bypass.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files share one concern: composing the application, which means wiring repositories, domain services, use cases and controllers together. createApp.ts is the top-level composition root. It builds the shared stores (InMemoryProductRepository, InMemoryOrderRepository) and the shared StockReservationService, then hands them to buildOrderController from orderModule.ts. orderModule.ts holds only the order use-case wiring and accepts its dependencies as parameters instead of creating new stores. Each instance is created in one place, so no wiring rule is repeated in both files. createApp uses the orderModule abstraction rather than bypassing it. One small inconsistency: stock wiring (StockController with ListStockLevelsUseCase) is done inline in createApp, while order wiring has its own builder. That is a style asymmetry, not a split of concerns or a duplicated invariant, so it does not fail the rubric.
